chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man performing tawaf who joins two sets of seven circuits together. He said: If you wish, I can narrate to you from the people of al-Madīnah.
He said: So I said: No, by Allah, I have no need for that, may I be made your ransom. Rather, narrate to me that by which I practice religion before Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

He said: Do not join two sets of seven circuits together. Rather, each time you complete one set of seven circuits, perform two rakʿahs. As for the supererogatory tawaf, I have at times joined three and four. So I looked at him, and he said: Indeed, I am with these people.

key_terms.أَدِينُ: to practice as religion before Allah
key_terms.أُسْبُوعَيْنِ: two sets of seven circuits of tawaf
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: the two units of prayer performed after tawaf
key_terms.يَقْرُنُ: joining or combining one act with another

ai.seo_question: Can two sets of seven circuits in tawaf be joined together without praying between them?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning tawaf: one should not combine two obligatory sets of seven circuits without performing the two rakʿahs after each set. The Imam عليه السلام then distinguishes the ruling for supererogatory tawaf, in which combining multiple sets may sometimes occur.
